correctness.rationale: In the natural basis, Leibniz on e_v² gives D(e_f(v))=2a_vv e_f(v), forcing every image-indexed column to be diagonal. On e_v e_w=0, independence of distinct target basis vectors forces both cross coefficients to vanish unless v,w have the same target; for equal targets they are negatives of one another. Thus both vertices must be leaves for a nonzero off-diagonal entry. In characteristic different from two the diagonal recurrence has exactly one free parameter per cycle with 2^L=1, determines all incoming values uniquely, and makes each sibling leaf block scalar on its diagonal. Hence the diagonal subalgebra centralizes the skew blocks and different supports commute. In characteristic two the image diagonals vanish and leaf diagonals are free; transpose of a commutator of symmetric matrices is its negative, equal to itself here. These conditions are also sufficient by bilinearity. Dimensions and finite-field cardinalities follow, including the cases of empty leaf sets, singleton blocks and fixed points. In the star/chain comparison, eliminating noncycle coordinates in leaf-to-root order gives k[T]/(T²−T) in both cases, whereas sibling block sizes four and one give the stated distinct derivation dimensions.
residual_risks: The checker was not executed. Its finite prime-field test design and sampled brackets are separate from the all-field symbolic verification above.

evidence: Prop. 3.1 gives necessary-and-sufficient derivation equations under the paper's characteristic-zero default. Prop. 3.8 explicitly purports to address any field but only for dim A²=1 with nonzero square of the generating square; it requires every diagonal coefficient to vanish.
The directed twin-free result is characteristic zero; the adjacency-algebra twin and complex rank-based studies do not state the nonperfect all-characteristic endofunction classification.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For e_0²=e_1²=e_0 over characteristic two, the rank-one hypotheses of Prop. 3.8 hold and D(e_0)=0, D(e_1)=e_1 satisfies all Leibniz equations. The leaf diagonal is nevertheless nonzero. The proof there drops the factor 2 in inferring that diagonal coefficients vanish; its printed arbitrary-field result cannot be used as covering the characteristic-two claim.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The coefficient identities do not themselves specify the structure of their solution Lie algebra. The surviving step solves the cyclic and tree diagonal constraints simultaneously, proves sibling off-diagonal support and proves that the odd-characteristic summand is central, while identifying the loss of the leaf diagonal constraint at 2. Neither the perfect theorem nor acyclic theorem on its own applies to a connected component with both a cycle and incoming trees.

evidence: The indexed nilpotent functional-square theorem has weighted orthogonal leaf blocks but assumes an acyclic directed graph and characteristic zero, allows zero basis squares, and has additional sink factors.
The perfect evolution-algebra theorem computes diagonal derivations from component balances.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A nonempty finite total endofunction has a directed cycle in each component and no zero square; the nilpotent acyclic formulation cannot be substituted directly. Perfectness E²=E is equivalent to surjectivity of f, hence bijectivity, which removes all leaf blocks. On these cycles the balance criterion is exactly the stated resonance condition, so that specialization is covered.

originality.rationale: Credit the simultaneous explicit Lie classification on nonbijective unweighted endofunctions over arbitrary fields. Earlier work covers the general Leibniz equations, characteristic-zero sibling mechanisms (including acyclic functional-square formulas), some rank-one cases in odd characteristic, and the perfect/bijective cycle result. None of the inspected statements covers the combined nonperfect cyclic case and characteristic-two symmetric blocks. The strongest apparent all-field rank-one comparison has a characteristic-two error as printed and does not cover image ranks greater than one even aside from that error.
residual_risks: A closed form using different terminology or a more general nonperfect Lie structure theorem was not ruled out exhaustively. Novelty is credited to the combined explicit classification, not to the separately covered ingredients.

value.rationale: The derivation Lie algebra is a natural structural invariant. The decomposition reads it directly from the functional graph, distinguishes the actual Lie bracket from a mere rank of Leibniz equations, and identifies a substantive characteristic-two change, not only a parameter substitution. It also explains why the star and chain can have the same idempotent scheme but different derivation dimensions. No priority is claimed for that example in isolation.
residual_risks: This invariant does not reconstruct the functional graph, and the audit does not extend the classification to weighted functional algebras or imply that each leaf factor is centerless.
